profile.headline: Embedded Software Engineer | Always looking to expand my knowledge
profile.summary:
Early on in my life I have always had the knack for tinkering and building. From getting my first LED to turn on to solving my first software bug I have enjoyed the problem solving. I choose to start my learning as a computer engineer at the University of Marquette. There I got exposed to interdisciplinary   development through SAE Baja and ways to further grow my drive to learn. I was given the opportunity to learn real learn software engineering through my time at Milwaukee Tool and Astronautics Corp of America. Since starting my position at Astronautics I have been exposed to many new and exciting tools, concepts, and people. I am always trying to learn from my coworkers who all come from different walks of life that show that in their development style. There I have been able to learn better ways to create reusable C code, create proper software tests to thoroughly test software and system functionality. Outside of the coding improvements I have gained at Astronautics they taught me how to be a better software engineer through the use of agile development, methods to debug, and when to reach out to coworkers for help.

Everyday I look to learn new things to further my knowledge of base. Whether that be through my day to day at work or trying something new for my personal projects.

positions.title: Embedded Software Engineer
positions.description:
Working at Astronautics I have been exposed to industry level embedded programming in C. Much of my time spent their has been writing low level device drivers for our development boards. In addition I have spent time writing testing software to allow the software engineering team to test our programs by peeking into the memory space of our microcontroller. This problem allows us to stop the microprocessor and read or modify values in memory to debug. Since this program lives off the chip it doesn't impede on the microprocessor's work.
As I have become more comfortable with the aerospace industry I have been spending more of my time at work becoming familiar with DO178 system design. I have been getting my feet wet with the DO178C flow of software requirements to software testing requirements to actual code.

positions.title: Software Engineering
positions.description: At my time at Milwaukee Electric Tool I was placed on a project to automatic the testing of existing or in progress battery system designs. The automated testers allows for the battery development team to test their current designs to see how incremental changes affected the product. If someone wanted to test their battery pcb or firmware they hook it up to the tester and run a suite of automated tests. The test would run through a range of possible situations a battery pack could experience in the real world and some edge cases. The system was modular so as Milwaukee Tool changed their battery designs the system could handle it

positions.title: Intern
positions.description: I worked various jobs from programming Zeiss CMM's, Keyence Imaging Devices, and Universal Robot arms to preparing data in Excel. In addition to odd jobs I helped revamp the quality control tool inventory system that is still in use today. It streamlined how machine operators get the tools they need and ensures the tools are calibrated.
